description: 🕵️‍♂️ Collect a dossier on a person by username from 6K websites

summary.one_liner: Maigret is a Python command-line tool (with a web UI and library API) that collects a dossier on a person by username, checking for accounts across thousands of websites.
summary.what_it_does: Given a username, Maigret checks whether accounts exist on a large set of sites (the README says 5,900 sites; a default run checks the 500 highest-ranked by traffic, and -a scans everything). It extracts available information from profile pages and site APIs, including links to other accounts, and runs recursive searches using discovered usernames and IDs. Results can be filtered by tags such as category or country, and exported as HTML, PDF, XMind, JSON, CSV, TXT, graph, or Neo4j Cypher. It can also route checks through a proxy, Tor, or I2P, and includes an opt-in AI mode that summarizes findings via an OpenAI-compatible API. The site database auto-updates from GitHub once per day, with a built-in fallback when offline.
use_cases: finding accounts a person uses across sites
building a graph of linked online identities
generating reports of username search results
notable: Searches by username only, with no API keys required for core use
Recursive search that follows usernames and IDs discovered on profile pages
Embeddable as an async Python library
Works with Tor and I2P sites and can check domains
Optional web UI showing results as a graph, plus Windows standalone exe and Snap packages
caveats: Site checks break over time and need ongoing maintenance, per the README's commercial-use section
Cloudflare bypass is experimented and its configuration may change without backward-compatibility guarantees
Tor and I2P daemons must be started separately; Maigret does not manage them
Snap package is strictly confined and can only write inside the home directory
The README is intended for educational and lawful use only and places compliance responsibility on the user
keywords: check which sites use my name
